howItWorks.metaDescription: From sign-up to a first shipped project: how parents set up accounts, how lessons work and how children stay motivated.
howItWorks.title: How it works
howItWorks.subtitle: Parents set things up. Children learn by doing. Everyone can see the progress.
howItWorks.setup: Sign up with your email, then add each child. You choose their nickname, preset avatar and password, and what they may share.
howItWorks.lessonTitle: Your child learns in short steps
howItWorks.lesson: Every lesson has a short video, a clear explanation and “try it” steps in a code editor that runs in the browser. There is nothing to install.
howItWorks.check: Your child gets feedback straight away. When something isn't right, a hint in their own language points the way, without giving the answer away.
howItWorks.projectTitle: Every module ends with a real project
howItWorks.project: Your child plans, builds and ships a project to their portfolio. The portfolio is private; with Premium, you can share it with a link.
howItWorks.watch: A short video introduces one idea at a time.
howItWorks.read: A clear explanation with examples, in your child's language.
howItWorks.try: Small coding steps in the browser, checked right away.
howItWorks.motivation: Rewards encourage a little practice often, not endless screen time.
howItWorks.xp: XP and levels for every step and project
howItWorks.badges: Badges for new skills and shipped projects
howItWorks.streaks: Daily streaks that reward regular practice
howItWorks.boards: Weekly leaderboards with nicknames and preset avatars only. Public boards appear only if you switch them on.
howItWorks.parents: Your parent dashboard shows what your child has learned and shipped. You can change settings or delete the account at any time.
howItWorks.languages: Lessons, hints and every screen are in English, Arabic and Urdu. Code words stay in English, just like in professional code.

safety.metaDescription: Parents in charge, nicknames and preset avatars only, no chat, code in a locked-down sandbox, as little data as possible, no ads and no trackers.
safety.title: Our safety promises
safety.subtitle: Children should be able to learn to code without the risks of social media. These are the promises we make to every family.
safety.parents: Only a parent can create a child's account; children never sign up alone. You choose the nickname, avatar and password, and you can change them or delete the account at any time.
safety.anonymous: Children appear with a nickname and one of our preset avatars. No photos, no real names, no schools.
safety.noChat: No adult can message a child, and children can’t message each other one to one. They talk only in moderated rooms for their team, class or event: under-13s use ready-made phrases, and parents can read along.
safety.boards: Weekly leaderboards show only a nickname, an avatar and XP. Public boards appear only if a parent switches them on.
safety.sandboxTitle: Code runs in a locked-down sandbox
safety.sandbox: Students' code runs in a separate, locked-down sandbox on its own domain. It can't see anyone's account or send data anywhere.
safety.data: We only keep what learning needs, and nothing for advertising. For a child, that is a nickname, a year of birth and a country.
safety.noAds: There are no adverts and no tracking scripts, in the app or on this website. The only cookie here remembers your language.
safety.details: The web app has our full safety page and privacy policy.
safety.report: Tell us straight away by replying to any email from us. A person reads every message, and safety reports come first.

about.metaDescription: Why we are building a safe coding school for children in Pakistan, Egypt, the UAE and Saudi Arabia.
about.title: Why we started {brand}
about.story1: We grew up between languages. At school we learned in one, at home we spoke another, and when we discovered programming, every tutorial was in English.
about.story2: We saw how much faster children learn when an idea is explained in the language they think in, and how often they give up when it isn't. We also saw coding apps for children borrow the worst habits of social media: chat with strangers, public profiles and adverts.
about.story3: So we are building the school we wanted for our own families: short lessons in English, Arabic and Urdu, real projects from the first week, and parents in charge of every account.
about.story4: We are starting small, with the Builder track for ages 13 to 16 in Pakistan, Egypt, the UAE and Saudi Arabia. We read every message families send us.
about.valueLanguage: Children learn best in their own language.
about.valueReal: Building real projects beats endless quizzes.
about.valueSafe: Safety isn't a feature. It is where we start.
about.valueFair: Prices should be fair in every country we serve.

faq.metaDescription: Answers for parents: ages, lessons, languages, safety, devices, prices and payment.
faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.subtitle: Can't find your answer? Join the waitlist and reply to our email. A person reads every message.
faq.agesA: The Builder track is for children aged 13 to 16 and is open now. Explorer (ages 9 to 12, block coding) and Pro (older teens) are coming later.
faq.experienceQ: Does my child need any coding experience?
faq.experienceA: No. Builder starts with the very first HTML tag. Short steps and hints make sure nobody stays stuck for long.
faq.lessonsQ: What does a lesson look like?
faq.lessonsA: A short video, a clear explanation and a few “try it” steps in a code editor in the browser. Every step is checked automatically, with hints in your child's language.
faq.languagesQ: Which languages are the lessons in?
faq.languagesA: English, Arabic and Urdu, and your child can switch at any time. Code words stay in English, as in professional code.
faq.signUpQ: Can my child sign up alone?
faq.signUpA: No. Only a parent or guardian can create a child's account. You choose the nickname, avatar and password, and you can delete the account at any time.
faq.safetyQ: How do you keep children safe?
faq.safetyA: Nicknames and preset avatars only, no chat of any kind, leaderboards that stay private unless you switch them on, and code that runs in a locked-down sandbox. No ads and no trackers.
faq.devicesA: A computer or tablet with a modern web browser and an internet connection. A keyboard helps. There is nothing to install.
faq.priceA: The Free plan includes the first lessons. Premium unlocks everything. Every new student gets a {days}-day Premium trial, and families get {percent}% off from the second child.
faq.paymentA: By card, processed securely by Stripe. In some countries you can also pay by bank transfer or mobile wallet.
faq.trialQ: What happens when the trial ends?
faq.trialA: Your child moves to the Free plan unless you choose Premium. The projects they shipped stay in their portfolio.

one.body: Describe the project below. We reply within a few working days, and say so kindly when a project isn’t a good fit for students.

two.title: Agree on scope and price

promises.code: Students are paid fairly: half of what you pay goes to the students who did the work.
